title: SSH transport for remote provisioning — shell out to system ssh/scp
decision: The remote-provisioning flow talks to target hosts by shelling out to the system `ssh` and `scp` binaries via `child_process.execFile` with strict argument arrays. It does not embed an npm SSH library (e.g., `ssh2`). All ssh/scp invocations pass every user-derived value as a distinct argv element with input validated against strict character-class regexes (`HOST_RE`, `USER_RE`, path allowlists); no argument reaches a shell interpreter.

context.task_description: Sprint 21 needs to install and start a daemon on a fresh Linux host, upload a tarball, run systemctl commands, and read a file — all from the client machine over SSH.
assumptions: Target users already have a working SSH setup (agent, keys, known_hosts) to their servers
Adding a new native/wasm dependency for SSH is a maintenance and audit burden we can avoid
The 10-step install flow does not need low-level features like port forwarding, interactive shells, or long-lived multiplexed channels — one-shot commands suffice

options.label: Shell out to system ssh/scp (chosen)
options.description: Zero new npm deps. Automatic support for the user's existing SSH agent, keys, ~/.ssh/config, and known_hosts. Errors classified from stderr text. Interactive password prompts are disabled via BatchMode=yes.

options.label: Embed the `ssh2` npm package
options.description: Native-code addon; would let us implement password auth, richer error introspection, and streaming. Rejected: adds a large audited surface for features we don't need in v1, and duplicates ~/.ssh/config behavior we get for free by shelling out.

options.label: Use libssh via napi-rs bindings
options.description: Same tradeoffs as ssh2 with more integration risk on packaged builds.

rationale: For a v1 install flow that is fundamentally 'run 8 one-shot commands and one file transfer,' shell-out to `ssh`/`scp` is the shortest path with the smallest audit surface. It also inherits every improvement the user's SSH stack accumulates (new agent, new key algorithm, ProxyJump entries in ~/.ssh/config) without our code caring. Injection risk is bounded because every argv element is validated and no string ever reaches a shell — the `run(cmd)` path passes `cmd` as a single ssh argv, and while ssh joins it into a remote shell string, callers construct that string themselves with awareness of shell metacharacters (heredocs, `&&` chains, etc.). If v2 needs password auth we can revisit; ssh2 remains an option.

risk.rollback: Replace ssh-client.ts internals with an ssh2-based implementation; the exported API surface (`test`/`run`/`upload` + SshTarget/SshError) does not change, so remote-provisioner.ts is unaffected.

outcome.notes: Sprint 21 in flight. Verification: live provisioning against an Ubuntu VM completes without prompting for a password (BatchMode=yes), and stderr classifications produce clear error kinds for unreachable/auth-failed/host-key-unknown.
